title: Lockstep simulation in the second phase
statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be finite-state machines over the Boolean alphabet. Let $x,y$ be Boolean words, let $c$ be a configuration of $M_2$ on virtual input $y$, and let $b$ be a Boolean tag that is false at the left boundary of $c$'s input-head position and true at its right boundary. Choose any valid physical input-head position $p$ for $x$, arbitrary contents and head positions for the left tape block of $M_1$, and a number of steps $t\in\mathbb N$. Then there is a Boolean tag $b'$ satisfying the same boundary condition for the input-head position reached by $M_2$ after $t$ steps from $c$, such that the buffered composition run for $t$ steps from the second-phase configuration determined by $c,b,p$ and the chosen left-block data equals the second-phase configuration determined by the resulting configuration of $M_2$, tag $b'$, and the same $p$ and left-block data.
hypotheses_covered: $M_1,M_2$ are finite-state machines over Boolean symbols
$c$ is a configuration of $M_2$ on virtual input $y$
$b$ satisfies the boundary-tag condition at $c$'s input-head position
$p$ is a valid physical input-head position for $x
left-block tape contents and head positions are arbitrary
replaced:
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be machines over the Boolean alphabet with finitely many
states, let $c$ be a configuration of $M_2$ on a virtual input $y$, and let
$b$ be a Boolean tag valid for the virtual input-head position of $c$.  Fix a
position $p$ of the physical input head over the real input $x$, arbitrary
inactive contents and head positions for the left tape block, and a number of
steps $t$.  Then there exists a tag $b'$, valid for the input-head position
of the run of $M_2$ for $t$ steps from $c$, such that running the buffered
sequential composition of $M_1$ and $M_2$ for $t$ steps from the second-phase
embedding of $c$ with tag $b$ equals the second-phase embedding of that run
with tag $b'$, keeping $p$ and the inactive data unchanged.  Completed
outputs and absorbing halting are thereby preserved.
